text.p: Investors have bid to buy 3.5 times the amount of shares the Egyptian state will auction in PACHIN/Paints and Chemical Industries after the offer deadline was extended, the agent for the sale said on Sunday.
The state offered 1.3125 million shares or 13.125 percent of PACHIN to investors in December.

The offer closed on December 25 more than twice oversubscribed but the state decided to extend the deadline for bids until January 9 to give investors more time after the Christmas and New Year holidays.
"We now have quite a few institutional and foreign investors taking part in the offer," said Fatma Lotfy, general manager for investment at Commercial International Bank.
She said the state had also scrapped the minimum price of 137.99 pounds a share and left investors to decide the price they wanted to pay.

"It's competitive bidding...The state will give those who have paid the highest price all the shares they have asked for and then it will move on to the next highest price until all the shares are over," she said.
Lotfy said she expected the state to stick to the quantity it had offered and not increase the tranche as in previous oversubscribed share offers.
"If they do increase the share tranche then it will be at a later time," she added. "They'll stay with the quantity."

The state still owns 87.5 percent of the 10 million shares in PACHIN. Some of the firm's shares were privatised several years ago and were trading on the Egyptian stock exchange at 124 pounds on Sunday morning.
